# Resource: stripe_issuing_cardholder

A person or business that Issuing cards are issued to. Stripe issues cards only for a platform's connected accounts, so manage cardholders through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is a connected account with the `card_issuing` capability active. Stripe reviews a new cardholder before its cards can be activated: `requirements.disabled_reason` reads `under_review` until then.

~> Stripe cannot delete a cardholder, so `terraform destroy` sets its `status` to `inactive` and leaves it on the connected account. Changing `name` or `type` replaces the cardholder, which leaves the old one inactive.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "issuing_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A connected account with the card_issuing capability active."
}

# Issuing runs on a connected account, so a second provider configuration acts on it.
provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "issuing"
  stripe_account = var.issuing_account
}

resource "stripe_issuing_cardholder" "jenny" {
  provider     = stripe.issuing
  type         = "individual"
  name         = "Jenny Rosen"
  email        = "jenny.rosen@example.com"
  phone_number = "+18008675309"

  individual = {
    first_name = "Jenny"
    last_name  = "Rosen"
    dob        = { day = 1, month = 1, year = 1990 }
    card_issuing = {
      user_terms_acceptance = { date = 1609459200, ip = "8.8.8.8" }
    }
  }

  billing = {
    address = {
      line1       = "354 Oyster Point Blvd"
      city        = "South San Francisco"
      state       = "CA"
      postal_code = "94080"
      country     = "US"
    }
  }

  spending_controls = {
    spending_limits = [{ amount = 50000, interval = "monthly" }]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `billing` - (Required) The cardholder's billing address. See [`billing`](#billing) below.
* `name` - (Required) The cardholder's name. This will be printed on cards issued to them. The maximum length of this field is 24 characters. This field cannot contain any special characters or numbers. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `company` - (Optional) Additional information about a `company` cardholder. See [`company`](#company) below.
* `email` - (Optional) The cardholder's email address.
* `individual` - (Optional) Additional information about an `individual` cardholder. See [`individual`](#individual) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `phone_number` - (Optional) The cardholder's phone number. This will be transformed to [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) if it is not provided in that format already. This is required for all cardholders who will be creating EU cards. See the [3D Secure documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/3d-secure#when-is-3d-secure-applied) for more details.
* `preferred_locales` - (Optional) The cardholder’s preferred locales (languages), ordered by preference. Locales can be `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, or `it`. This changes the language of the [3D Secure flow](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/3d-secure) and one-time password messages sent to the cardholder.
* `spending_controls` - (Optional) Rules that control spending across this cardholder's cards. Refer to our [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/controls/spending-controls) for more details. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`spending_controls`](#spending_controls) below.
* `status` - (Optional) Specifies whether to permit authorizations on this cardholder's cards. Defaults to `active`. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `type` - (Optional) One of `individual` or `company`. See [Choose a cardholder type](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/other/choose-cardholder) for more details. Possible values: `company`, `individual`. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="billing"></a>
### `billing`

The `billing` attribute supports:

* `address` - (Required) See [`billing.address`](#billing.address) below.

<a id="billing.address"></a>
### `billing.address`

The `billing.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Required) City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - (Required) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - (Required) Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - (Required) ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="company"></a>
### `company`

The `company` attribute supports:

* `tax_id` - (Optional, Sensitive)
* `tax_id_provided` - (Read-Only) Whether the company's business ID number was provided.

<a id="individual"></a>
### `individual`

The `individual` attribute supports:

* `card_issuing` - (Optional) Information related to the card_issuing program for this cardholder. See [`individual.card_issuing`](#individual.card_issuing) below.
* `dob` - (Optional) The date of birth of this cardholder. See [`individual.dob`](#individual.dob) below.
* `first_name` - (Optional) The first name of this cardholder. Required before activating Cards. This field cannot contain any numbers, special characters (except periods, commas, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes) or non-latin letters.
* `last_name` - (Optional) The last name of this cardholder. Required before activating Cards. This field cannot contain any numbers, special characters (except periods, commas, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes) or non-latin letters.
* `verification` - (Optional) Government-issued ID document for this cardholder. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`individual.verification`](#individual.verification) below.

<a id="individual.card_issuing"></a>
### `individual.card_issuing`

The `individual.card_issuing` attribute supports:

* `user_terms_acceptance` - (Optional) Information about cardholder acceptance of Celtic [Authorized User Terms](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/compliance-us#issuing-terms). Required for cards backed by a Celtic program. See [`individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance`](#individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance) below.

<a id="individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance"></a>
### `individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance`

The `individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance` attribute supports:

* `date` - (Optional) The Unix timestamp marking when the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.
* `ip` - (Optional) The IP address from which the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.
* `user_agent` - (Optional) The user agent of the browser from which the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.

<a id="individual.dob"></a>
### `individual.dob`

The `individual.dob` attribute supports:

* `day` - (Required) The day of birth, between 1 and 31.
* `month` - (Required) The month of birth, between 1 and 12.
* `year` - (Required) The four-digit year of birth.

<a id="individual.verification"></a>
### `individual.verification`

The `individual.verification` attribute supports:

* `document` - (Optional) An identifying document, either a passport or local ID card. See [`individual.verification.document`](#individual.verification.document) below.

<a id="individual.verification.document"></a>
### `individual.verification.document`

The `individual.verification.document` attribute supports:

* `back` - (Optional) The back of a document returned by a [file upload](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_file) with a `purpose` value of `identity_document`.
* `front` - (Optional) The front of a document returned by a [file upload](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_file) with a `purpose` value of `identity_document`.

<a id="spending_controls"></a>
### `spending_controls`

The `spending_controls` attribute supports:

* `allowed_card_presences` - (Optional) Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be allowed. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. All other statuses will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `allowed_categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to allow. All other categories will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_categories`.
* `allowed_merchant_countries` - (Optional) Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be allowed. Authorizations from merchants in all other countries will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `blocked_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_card_presences` - (Optional) Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be declined. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. Cannot be set with `allowed_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to decline. All other categories will be allowed. Cannot be set with `allowed_categories`.
* `blocked_merchant_countries` - (Optional) Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `allowed_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `spending_limits` - (Optional) Limit spending with amount-based rules that apply across this cardholder's cards. See [`spending_controls.spending_limits`](#spending_controls.spending_limits) below.
* `spending_limits_currency` - (Optional) Currency of the amounts within `spending_limits`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.

<a id="spending_controls.spending_limits"></a>
### `spending_controls.spending_limits`

The `spending_controls.spending_limits` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - (Required) Maximum amount allowed to spend per interval. This amount is in the card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) this limit applies to. Omitting this field will apply the limit to all categories.
* `interval` - (Required) Interval (or event) to which the amount applies. Possible values: `all_time`, `daily`, `monthly`, `per_authorization`, `weekly`, `yearly`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `requirements` - See [`requirements`](#requirements) below.

<a id="requirements"></a>
### `requirements`

The `requirements` attribute supports:

* `disabled_reason` - If `disabled_reason` is present, all cards will decline authorizations with `cardholder_verification_required` reason. Possible values: `listed`, `rejected.listed`, `requirements.past_due`, `under_review`.
* `past_due` - Array of fields that need to be collected in order to verify and re-enable the cardholder.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

Run the import where the resource's `provider` acts on the connected account that holds it.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an issuing cardholder using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_issuing_cardholder.jenny
  id = "ich_1MsKAB2eZvKYlo2C3eZ2BdvK"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_issuing_cardholder.jenny
  identity = {
    id = "ich_1MsKAB2eZvKYlo2C3eZ2BdvK"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the issuing cardholder.

Using `terraform import`, import an issuing cardholder using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_issuing_cardholder.jenny ich_1MsKAB2eZvKYlo2C3eZ2BdvK
```

-> Stripe never returns a company's `tax_id`, so an imported cardholder has none in state, and a configuration that sets `company.tax_id` plans an update that sends it again.
